correctness.rationale: For each finite set of skeleton edges and each nonzero rational polynomial, nonvanishing is open. Density follows by first perturbing the finite restriction into the strict finite metric cone, avoiding the polynomial zero set there, and then applying exact metric interpolation on the finite closed set. Countability and the Baire property give the dense G_delta theorem. The Euclidean strata are closed by finite Gram-kernel positivity and rank conditions and nowhere dense by perturbing an (m+2)-point Cayley--Menger determinant away from zero. Algebraic independence of raw distances also makes their squares algebraically independent, yielding the rigidity-matroid consequences.

value.rationale: The result isolates a natural way to retain maximal algebraic freedom of distances on connected or positive-dimensional spaces, and it turns that freedom into exact finite-dimensional Euclidean and rigidity-matroid obstructions. The fixed-skeleton formulation is useful precisely where full algebraic independence is topologically unavailable.

final_claim: For every metrizable space and every fixed countable subset, compatible metrics whose skeleton distances are algebraically independent form a dense \(G_\delta\) set; this yields closed nowhere-dense fixed-dimensional Euclidean strata and the stated Cayley--Menger rigidity obstructions.
limitations: Only a fixed countable skeleton is forced to have algebraically independent distances; Euclidean conclusions concern exact isometric embeddings; rigidity-matroid independence is necessary rather than sufficient; the result is qualitative.
